*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /var/folders/zm/8n69b_ld4d17cf77mbq1f0g00000gn/T/opencode/binden-workspace-spec.md
+## Problem Statement
+
+The nonprofit needs a simpler way to onboard people, maintain their Google Workspace information, and offboard departing users. Today, this work requires administrators to coordinate requests and perform management through Google's tools, while ordinary users lack a suitable place to request changes to their own contact information.
+
+The application must not introduce a second authoritative user directory or a conflicting permission system. Applicants need to request accounts before they have managed Google identities; existing Workspace users must see only their own information; administrators must act within their actual Google privileges. The organization is small, so operating cost and administrative effort must remain low.
+
+The codebase currently provides a Next.js application scaffold and a configured shadcn/Tailwind UI. Drizzle and Neon dependencies are installed, but authentication, persistence, Workspace integrations, workflows, and application tests are not implemented.
+
+## Solution
+
+Provide one application for the nonprofit's Workspace organization, with public email-verified signup, Google-backed sign-in for existing Workspace users, administrator review queues, user and group administration, and suspension-first offboarding.
+
+Applicants submit a signup request without needing a personal Google account. An administrator reviews it, confirms a programmatically generated Workspace email suggestion, and accepts or rejects it. Acceptance creates the managed account and explicitly selected group memberships. Account handover uses Google's existing-user password-reset email flow in the Admin console. Rejected requests are deleted after outcome notification.
+
+Workspace users view their own Google-authoritative profile and submit contact email or phone changes for approval. An administrator approves the reviewed request and the application writes to Google using that administrator's OAuth credentials. This preserves Google's permission enforcement without domain-wide delegation or application-owned administrator roles.
+
+Administrators manage users and Google Groups within their Google privileges, including member, manager, and owner memberships. Suspension is the normal offboarding action; deletion is separate and requires confirmation that data disposition was resolved in Google's Admin console.
+
+Verification, outcome, and review-notification emails use a dedicated Workspace mailbox. Deploy on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres for application-owned workflow data, keeping the architecture inexpensive and leaving provider tier management to the organization.
+
+## User Stories
+
+### Applicants and onboarding
+
+1. As an applicant, I want to request a Workspace account without already having one, so that I can join the organization.
+2. As an applicant, I want to apply without needing a personal Google account, so that account eligibility does not depend on my choice of email provider.
+3. As an applicant, I want to provide my given name, family name, and contact email, so that an administrator has the required information to review my signup request.
+4. As an applicant, I want to provide an optional phone number, so that the organization can contact me through an additional channel if needed.
+5. As an applicant, I want clear validation feedback, so that I can correct missing or invalid information before submission.
+6. As an applicant, I want to verify my contact email, so that the organization knows I can receive account-related messages there.
+7. As an applicant, I want confirmation that my verified signup request was submitted, so that I know it is awaiting administrator review.
+8. As an applicant, I want the organization to assign my Workspace email, so that account addresses follow its conventions rather than applicant preferences.
+9. As an applicant, I want an email outcome for my signup request, so that I know whether I have been accepted or rejected without an applicant dashboard.
+10. As an approved applicant, I want a Google-generated password-reset link at an address I can already access, so that I can obtain access to my new account without receiving a plaintext password.
+11. As an approved applicant, I want to choose a new password during account handover, so that my ongoing access does not depend on a temporary provisioning password.
+12. As a rejected applicant, I want my submitted profile deleted after outcome notification, so that the application does not retain unnecessary applicant information.
+
+### Administrator review and provisioning
+
+13. As an administrator, I want a review queue of verified signup requests, so that I can evaluate applicants in one place.
+14. As an administrator, I want an email notification when a verified signup request is submitted, so that I do not have to discover new requests by repeatedly checking the application.
+15. As an administrator, I want to view the information submitted by an applicant, so that I can decide whether to accept the signup request.
+16. As an administrator, I want a programmatically generated Workspace email suggestion, so that creating an account requires less manual work.
+17. As an administrator, I want to confirm or edit the generated suggestion and check its availability, so that the resulting Workspace address is appropriate and does not conflict with an existing account.
+18. As an administrator, I want acceptance to create the user in Google Workspace, so that approval results in a managed account rather than a separate application-only user.
+19. As an administrator, I want to reject a signup request and notify the applicant, so that unsuitable requests can be resolved and their submitted data removed.
+20. As an administrator, I want to select optional initial groups explicitly, so that new users receive only intended memberships.
+21. As an administrator, I want initial memberships to default to member, so that management authority is not granted accidentally.
+22. As an administrator, I want to select manager or owner roles explicitly when authorized, so that onboarding can establish the intended group responsibilities.
+23. As an administrator, I want to distinguish account creation, membership assignment, and account handover completion, so that I can finish partially completed onboarding correctly.
+24. As an administrator, I want failed provisioning to remain recoverable, so that temporary Google or database failures do not lose an accepted applicant's request.
+25. As an administrator, I want repeated approval or retry attempts not to create duplicate accounts, so that recovery is safe.
+26. As an administrator, I want an email collision never to attach an applicant to an existing account, so that an applicant cannot receive someone else's identity.
+27. As an administrator, I want unreviewed signup requests to expire after 30 days, so that the review queue does not retain obsolete applications indefinitely.
+28. As an administrator, I want successful applicant form data removed after provisioning and handover, so that only the minimal provisioning record remains.
+
+### Workspace user self-service
+
+29. As a Workspace user, I want to sign in with my managed Google identity, so that I do not need another password or application account.
+30. As a Workspace user, I want my displayed profile to come from Google Workspace, so that changes made through Google's tools are reflected rather than contradicted by an application copy.
+31. As a Workspace user, I want to see only my own permitted profile and request, so that other users' information remains private.
+32. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact email change, so that the organization can reach me at the right address.
+33. As a Workspace user, I want to verify a replacement contact email, so that an administrator can approve a reachable address.
+34. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact phone change, so that the organization can maintain accurate contact information.
+35. As a Workspace user, I want to see my pending profile change request separately from my current profile, so that I understand which values are proposed and which are already authoritative in Google.
+36. As a Workspace user, I want a newer submission to replace my one pending request, so that an administrator reviews my latest intended changes.
+37. As a Workspace user, I want an email outcome for my profile change request, so that I know whether the changes were accepted or rejected.
+38. As a Workspace user, I want rejection to leave my Google profile unchanged, so that unapproved proposals cannot alter my account.
+39. As a Workspace user, I want my application access to stop after my account is suspended or deleted, so that application sessions do not bypass Workspace account status.
+
+### Profile approval and permission enforcement
+
+40. As an administrator, I want to review pending profile change requests, so that contact changes can be approved without giving ordinary users Directory write authority.
+41. As an administrator, I want an email notification when a verified profile change request is submitted, so that I can respond without continuous polling.
+42. As an administrator, I want to approve or reject the entire reviewed request, so that the outcome is unambiguous.
+43. As an administrator, I want approval to apply only the request version I reviewed, so that a concurrent replacement cannot change what I authorize.
+44. As an administrator, I want approved changes to preserve unrelated Google contact entries and recovery settings, so that updating contact information does not damage other account data.
+45. As an administrator, I want management operations to execute under my Google OAuth credentials, so that Google enforces my privileges and resource restrictions.
+46. As an administrator, I want permission denials to be reported without escalation to another account, so that the application cannot bypass Google's authorization decisions.
+47. As an administrator, I want Google-side role changes to affect application permissions, so that the application does not retain stale administrator authority.
+
+### User administration and offboarding
+
+48. As an administrator, I want to list Workspace users within my authorized scope, so that I can find the accounts I manage.
+49. As an administrator, I want to view and edit Google-supported user information within my privileges, so that I can manage fields that ordinary users cannot change.
+50. As an administrator, I want to suspend a Workspace user, so that I can stop access while retaining the account and its data.
+51. As an administrator, I want to unsuspend a Workspace user when authorized, so that reversible offboarding can be undone.
+52. As an administrator, I want deletion to be a distinct, explicitly confirmed action after data disposition, so that permanent removal does not happen accidentally or before the organization has dealt with the user's data.
+
+### Group administration
+
+53. As an administrator, I want to list Google Groups, so that I can find the groups I am authorized to manage.
+54. As an administrator, I want to create a group and edit its basic details, so that the organization's group structure stays useful.
+55. As an administrator, I want to delete a group when authorized, so that obsolete groups can be removed.
+56. As an administrator, I want to inspect direct group memberships, so that I can understand who belongs to each group and in which role.
+57. As an administrator, I want to add or remove direct Workspace-user memberships, so that group access and mailing-list membership match organizational needs.
+58. As an administrator, I want to assign and change member, manager, and owner roles, so that group responsibilities are managed explicitly.
+59. As an administrator, I want unrelated existing group settings preserved, so that basic management does not unexpectedly change posting or privacy behavior.
+60. As an organization operator, I want group owner/manager roles and notification-group membership not to grant application-wide administrator authority, so that authorization remains tied to Google administrative privileges.
+
+### Operations, privacy, and usability
+
+61. As an organization operator, I want emails sent through a dedicated Workspace mailbox, so that notifications use an organization-controlled identity with send-only permission.
+62. As an organization operator, I want review notifications delivered to one configured Google Group, so that recipients can be managed through Google without an application role system.
+63. As an organization operator, I want notification emails to contain minimal personal information and a review link, so that submitted profiles and secrets are not distributed unnecessarily.
+64. As an organization operator, I want email failures to be visible and safely retryable, so that requests and outcomes do not disappear silently.
+65. As an organization operator, I want OAuth connections to report revocation or reconnection needs, so that failed credentials can be repaired without silently changing the acting identity.
+66. As an organization operator, I want workflow records separated from Google-authoritative profiles, so that the application does not create a second directory or permission system.
+67. As an organization operator, I want serverless hosting and a database that can become idle, so that a small workload has low ongoing cost.
+68. As an organization operator, I want provider tier management handled manually, so that the application does not introduce billing features or automatic upgrades.
+69. As an organization operator, I want public submissions and verification emails protected against invalid input and abuse, so that avoidable misuse does not consume limited resources.
+70. As an applicant or Workspace user, I want accessible forms and clear loading, success, and error states, so that I can complete workflows using the existing consistent UI.
+
+## Implementation Decisions
+
+### Domain and module interfaces
+
+- Preserve the agreed vocabulary: applicant, signup request, Workspace user, administrator, contact email, Workspace email, profile change request, account handover, suspension, deletion, group, group membership, group manager, group owner, and initial group membership.
+- Support one Workspace organization. A personal Google account used elsewhere is not the applicant's new managed identity.
+- Extend the existing application with public signup, own-profile self-service, administrator review, user administration, and group administration. Expose their behavior through the running application's browser-facing interface rather than inventing a separate public management API.
+- Keep request handling, authorization, persistence, and Google operations behind that application interface. Reuse existing patterns and installed dependencies; do not create one-to-one pass-through modules or speculative abstractions.
+- Trust-boundary contracts validate inputs, authenticated identity, ownership, current authority, request version, and completion state on the server. Browser-provided identifiers never establish ownership or privileges.
+
+### Identity and Google access
+
+- Existing Workspace users authenticate through Google. Validate token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and applicable state/nonce protections; enforce organizational membership from verified identity claims, not an email suffix or sign-in UI hint.
+- Bind the authenticated identity to a stable Google Directory user identifier server-side. Handle primary-email changes safely. Do not assume undocumented equality between the OpenID Connect subject and the Directory user identifier.
+- Re-evaluate account status for protected access so suspension or deletion cannot be bypassed by a previously issued application session. Google-side privilege changes must also be respected.
+- Ordinary-user consent does not authorize Directory writes. Self-service therefore submits approval requests rather than writing directly to Google.
+- Use the acting administrator's OAuth connection for administrative reads and writes. Google enforces that account's action, resource, and organizational-unit restrictions. Do not use a stronger shared writer, infer authority from broad administrator flags alone, or retry a denial under another identity.
+- Request the user-management and group-management Directory scopes required by the selected operations. Add read-only role inspection only when the interface needs it and the calling account is authorized. If roles are interpreted, account for indirect assignments, privilege hierarchy, and assignment scope.
+- Ordinary-user Directory reads expose domain-public information and do not document a full own-profile exception. Provide private own-profile display through an isolated backend OAuth reader with the Directory user read-only scope and a delegated account limited to Users Read in relevant organizational units. Derive the target from the authenticated session and return only permitted own-profile fields. This reader performs no writes and does not expand administrator listings beyond the acting administrator's scope.
+- Keep reader, acting-administrator, and notification-sender grants isolated by purpose, including protection against accidentally accumulating write grants on the reader. Credentials remain server-side and protected; revoked or expired connections have explicit reconnection behavior.
+- Do not use domain-wide delegation initially. This avoids its broad impersonation authority while accepting administrator approval delays for contact changes.
+
+### Signup, approval, and account handover
+
+- Require given name, family name, and verified contact email; phone is optional. Email verification precedes entry into the review queue. There is no applicant login/dashboard.
+- Generate Workspace email suggestions using the agreed given.family convention. The reviewing administrator confirms or edits them; applicants have no address-selection interface. Validate suggestions against Google naming rules and availability without connecting a collision to an existing user.
+- Acceptance provisions through Google under the approving administrator's authority. Initial group memberships are optional and explicit, with member as the default and manager/owner as deliberate selections.
+- Generate a random temporary password only for the Google creation operation, require a password change, and do not retain or expose that password in workflow records, logs, or emails.
+- Account handover remains a manual Google Admin console operation: reset the existing user's password with required change enabled and email Google's reset link to an address the applicant can access. Track handover completion before purging successful applicant form data.
+- Distinguish account creation, initial membership completion, and account handover so failures can be recovered without repeating completed work or creating another account.
+- Reject stale or already-resolved review actions. Preserve sufficient progress to recover when an external operation succeeds but later database or notification work fails; do not claim a distributed atomic transaction across Google and Postgres.
+- Rejected requests are deleted after outcome notification. Unreviewed signup requests expire after 30 days. Successful applicant form data is removed after provisioning and handover; retain only a minimal provisioning record identifying the Google account and approving administrator.
+
+### Profile change requests
+
+- Users may propose contact email and phone changes only. Name, Workspace email, organizational assignments, memberships, account status, recovery fields, and security settings remain administrator-controlled.
+- Store proposals separately from the current Google profile. Verify a replacement contact email before approval; replacing it requires verification of the new proposal.
+- Allow at most one pending profile change request per Workspace user. A new submission replaces it. Enforce this constraint in persistence, not just the interface.
+- Approval/rejection applies to the whole reviewed request. Use request-version/concurrency protection so a replaced proposal cannot be approved with stale reviewed contents.
+- Approved values are written with the approving administrator's OAuth credentials. Contact email and phone belong in Google contact arrays, not the Workspace primary address or account-recovery fields.
+- Preserve unrelated contact-array entries when submitting complete desired arrays to Google. Show success only after the relevant Google write succeeds; rejection leaves the profile unchanged.
+- Notification failure after a successful write must not cause the write to be repeated as if it had failed.
+
+### User and group administration
+
+- Provide authorized user listing, profile editing, suspension, unsuspension, and deletion. Permission checks apply to each action and target, not merely access to an administrator screen.
+- Suspension is the standard offboarding action. Deletion requires distinct confirmation that data disposition has been resolved manually in Google's Admin console. Do not implement automated data transfer.
+- Provide basic Google Group listing, creation, detail editing, and deletion, plus direct membership inspection, addition, removal, and member/manager/owner role changes for Workspace users.
+- Preserve unrelated existing group settings. Group owner/manager roles do not automatically confer application administrator authority.
+- Paginate Google lists correctly. Treat Google permissions, propagation delays, resource conflicts, and missing records as actual external outcomes rather than silently bypassing them.
+
+### Persistence and recovery
+
+- Use Drizzle ORM with Neon Postgres for signup requests, email-verification evidence, pending profile change requests, workflow progress/versioning, minimal provisioning records, and necessary protected OAuth/session state.
+- Store only the fields and constraints required by those workflows: verified-contact binding, stable Google identifiers, expiry timestamps, request versions, completion/progress state, and notification retry state where needed.
+- Do not maintain an authoritative local copy of existing user profiles, group memberships, or administrator roles. Verification evidence does not make the application's contact value authoritative over Google.
+- Make review actions, cleanup, notification retries, and provisioning recovery safe under concurrent or repeated execution.
+- Enforce expiration when requests are viewed or acted on. Daily cleanup is sufficient for eventual removal; it must tolerate missed or duplicate scheduling rather than relying on an exact invocation time.
+- Accept Neon's native Free recovery initially, including its currently documented six-hour restore window for application-owned records. Independent backups are deferred; Google remains authoritative for managed Workspace data.
+
+### Email, UI, and deployment
+
+- Send verification, outcome, and administrator-notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with an offline OAuth grant limited to Gmail send permission and no Directory administrator privileges.
+- Send administrator notifications for verified signup and profile change submissions to one configured Google Group. Include a review-queue link and minimal personal information, never passwords, verification secrets, or full submitted profiles.
+- Notification-group membership controls delivery only. Configure posting permission and recipient subscriptions so the selected mailbox can reach reviewers; notification links still require authenticated, authorized review access.
+- Make email delivery failures visible and retryable without losing requests or repeating completed Google operations. Protect verification tokens and rate-limit public submissions and verification sending.
+- Use the existing preconfigured shadcn/Tailwind UI and accessible native form behavior. Include explicit pending, empty, denied, success, and failure states where the workflow requires them; no manually authored UI CSS.
+- Deploy the existing Next.js application on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres. Prefer serverless/on-demand execution and database scale-to-zero; avoid continuous polling and always-on infrastructure.
+- Provider plan selection, tier changes, and allowances are handled manually. Do not implement tier management, quota-based upgrades, or application billing.
+
+## Testing Decisions
+
+- **Approved primary seam:** the running application's browser-facing interface. Exercise real screens, server operations, validation, sessions, authorization, workflow transitions, and persistence through that interface. Keep one primary application-level seam rather than separate helper or UI-structure suites.
+- **Good tests assert external behavior:** what an actor can see or do, what request state is persisted, whether a Google operation occurs under the correct identity, and what notification is sent. Do not assert internal function calls, private module arrangement, component markup structure, or implementation-specific timing.
+- **Modules exercised:** the application module spanning signup, verification, identity/access, own-profile display, profile proposals, administrator review, user administration, group administration, account handover tracking, expiry, notification delivery, and recovery. Test these through their shared application interface, not individually invented testing interfaces.
+- **Database:** use an isolated real Postgres database with the actual Drizzle schema/migrations, so uniqueness, request replacement, concurrent approval, progress persistence, and cleanup are tested against real database behavior. Tests must not use production workflow records.
+- **External adapters:** control Google identity/OAuth, Directory, and Gmail responses at their external interfaces. Simulate permission denials, revoked credentials, propagation delay, conflicting/missing resources, successful writes followed by later failures, and notification failure. Keep production authentication and authorization enforcement active rather than adding bypasses solely for tests.
+- **Identity/privacy checks:** cover invalid or wrong-organization identities, arbitrary target identifiers, another user's request/profile access, private own-profile reads through the read-only connection, administrator scope restrictions, role revocation, suspension, and deletion while an application session exists.
+- **Signup checks:** cover required fields, email verification, absence of applicant email choice, programmatic suggestions and conflicts, acceptance/rejection, optional role-specific memberships, handover tracking, 30-day expiry, data removal, concurrent approval, and recovery without duplicate creation.
+- **Profile checks:** cover proposed versus authoritative values, replacement-email verification, one pending request, replacement during review, whole-request decisions, permission denial, unchanged Google data on rejection, preservation of unrelated contact/recovery fields, and retry after notification failure without repeating a completed write.
+- **Administration checks:** cover authorized user editing, suspend/unsuspend, deletion confirmation/data-disposition prerequisite, group creation/edit/deletion, and direct member/manager/owner changes. Ensure group roles and notification-group membership do not become application-wide permissions.
+- **Notification/retention checks:** assert verified submission notifications, minimal email contents, protected review links, outcomes, recoverable sending failures, cleanup idempotency, expiry enforcement even when cleanup is delayed, and successful/rejected applicant-data removal at the agreed points.
+- **Live integration check:** perform a small controlled check in the actual Workspace organization for delegated-admin creation authority, role/OU restrictions, private profile reads, member/manager/owner support, OAuth reconnection, and notification-group delivery. Verify the manual Google reset-email handover. Simulated Google responses cannot establish these tenant capabilities; use dedicated test accounts/resources for destructive checks.
+- **Prior art:** the repository has no application tests, configured test runner, or existing workflow seams to reuse. Reuse the real Next.js application interface and existing Drizzle/Neon setup; select only the minimal browser-test tooling needed to make these checks runnable.
+- **Required checks:** run the repository lint, formatting, and build checks alongside the meaningful workflow/authorization checks. Add lower-level tests only if a demonstrated behavior cannot be reliably covered through the approved seam.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Multiple independent Workspace organizations or a multi-tenant product.
+- Applicant Google login, applicant dashboards, or applicant-selected Workspace addresses.
+- Immediate ordinary-user Directory writes without administrator approval.
+- Application-owned administrator roles, duplicated authoritative profiles/memberships, shared stronger write credentials, or domain-wide delegation.
+- User self-service changes to names, Workspace email, organizational assignments, group memberships, account status, recovery fields, or security settings.
+- Automatic initial group memberships or implicit grants of owner/manager authority.
+- Nested-group management, external-member management, and a group posting/privacy settings editor.
+- Automated data transfer, automated password-reset-link generation through undocumented APIs, plaintext-password delivery, or fully automated account handover.
+- Notifications that expose full submitted profiles or make their recipients authorized reviewers by membership alone.
+- Provider tier management, automatic paid upgrades, billing features, always-on workers, or continuous review-queue polling.
+- Independent backups beyond the accepted Neon native recovery initially.
+- Speculative abstractions, a separate public management API, exhaustive per-helper tests, or a UI redesign that replaces the configured shadcn system.
+
+## Further Notes
+
+- The owner approved the product decisions and the proposed primary testing seam. This specification synthesizes that agreement rather than reopening product questions.
+- This issue is the canonical implementation specification. Preserve the agreed glossary and architectural rationale during implementation, and follow the repository worktree/stacked-PR workflow and installed Next.js documentation before writing framework code.
+- **Delegated-admin creation remains an integration check:** current Google documentation conflicts about creating users through the Directory API as a delegated administrator. Verify the intended role in the actual tenant before relying on it. If Google denies creation, an appropriately privileged administrator must perform the approval; never escalate silently.
+- **Group manager support:** validate Groups for Business availability and actual member/manager/owner behavior in the tenant.
+- **Recovery and cost:** Google-managed data and local pending workflow records have different recovery characteristics. The organization accepts native Neon recovery initially and manages provider tiers manually; free allowances are not an unlimited-operation guarantee.
+- **Manual handover is intentional:** Google account creation and the Admin console reset-email procedure are separate steps. Track the latter rather than declaring onboarding fully complete immediately after account creation.
+- Official references: [Directory users and non-admin access](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/manage-users), [Directory read views](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/get), [user creation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/insert), [user update semantics](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/update), [administrator privileges](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/administrator-privilege-definitions), [delegation trade-offs](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/domain-wide-delegation-best-practices), [Console password-reset handover](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/reset-a-users-password), [Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), and [Neon plans](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans).
*** End Patch

+## Problem Statement
+
+The nonprofit needs a simpler way to onboard people, maintain their Google Workspace information, and offboard departing users. Today, this work requires administrators to coordinate requests and perform management through Google's tools, while ordinary users lack a suitable place to request changes to their own contact information.
+
+The application must not introduce a second authoritative user directory or a conflicting permission system. Applicants need to request accounts before they have managed Google identities; existing Workspace users must see only their own information; administrators must act within their actual Google privileges. The organization is small, so operating cost and administrative effort must remain low.
+
+The codebase currently provides a Next.js application scaffold and a configured shadcn/Tailwind UI. Drizzle and Neon dependencies are installed, but authentication, persistence, Workspace integrations, workflows, and application tests are not implemented.
+
+## Solution
+
+Provide one application for the nonprofit's Workspace organization, with public email-verified signup, Google-backed sign-in for existing Workspace users, administrator review queues, user and group administration, and suspension-first offboarding.
+
+Applicants submit a signup request without needing a personal Google account. An administrator reviews it, confirms a programmatically generated Workspace email suggestion, and accepts or rejects it. Acceptance creates the managed account and explicitly selected group memberships. Account handover uses Google's existing-user password-reset email flow in the Admin console. Rejected requests are deleted after outcome notification.
+
+Workspace users view their own Google-authoritative profile and submit contact email or phone changes for approval. An administrator approves the reviewed request and the application writes to Google using that administrator's OAuth credentials. This preserves Google's permission enforcement without domain-wide delegation or application-owned administrator roles.
+
+Administrators manage users and Google Groups within their Google privileges, including member, manager, and owner memberships. Suspension is the normal offboarding action; deletion is separate and requires confirmation that data disposition was resolved in Google's Admin console.
+
+Verification, outcome, and review-notification emails use a dedicated Workspace mailbox. Deploy on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres for application-owned workflow data, keeping the architecture inexpensive and leaving provider tier management to the organization.
+
+## User Stories
+
+### Applicants and onboarding
+
+1. As an applicant, I want to request a Workspace account without already having one, so that I can join the organization.
+2. As an applicant, I want to apply without needing a personal Google account, so that account eligibility does not depend on my choice of email provider.
+3. As an applicant, I want to provide my given name, family name, and contact email, so that an administrator has the required information to review my signup request.
+4. As an applicant, I want to provide an optional phone number, so that the organization can contact me through an additional channel if needed.
+5. As an applicant, I want clear validation feedback, so that I can correct missing or invalid information before submission.
+6. As an applicant, I want to verify my contact email, so that the organization knows I can receive account-related messages there.
+7. As an applicant, I want confirmation that my verified signup request was submitted, so that I know it is awaiting administrator review.
+8. As an applicant, I want the organization to assign my Workspace email, so that account addresses follow its conventions rather than applicant preferences.
+9. As an applicant, I want an email outcome for my signup request, so that I know whether I have been accepted or rejected without an applicant dashboard.
+10. As an approved applicant, I want a Google-generated password-reset link at an address I can already access, so that I can obtain access to my new account without receiving a plaintext password.
+11. As an approved applicant, I want to choose a new password during account handover, so that my ongoing access does not depend on a temporary provisioning password.
+12. As a rejected applicant, I want my submitted profile deleted after outcome notification, so that the application does not retain unnecessary applicant information.
+
+### Administrator review and provisioning
+
+13. As an administrator, I want a review queue of verified signup requests, so that I can evaluate applicants in one place.
+14. As an administrator, I want an email notification when a verified signup request is submitted, so that I do not have to discover new requests by repeatedly checking the application.
+15. As an administrator, I want to view the information submitted by an applicant, so that I can decide whether to accept the signup request.
+16. As an administrator, I want a programmatically generated Workspace email suggestion, so that creating an account requires less manual work.
+17. As an administrator, I want to confirm or edit the generated suggestion and check its availability, so that the resulting Workspace address is appropriate and does not conflict with an existing account.
+18. As an administrator, I want acceptance to create the user in Google Workspace, so that approval results in a managed account rather than a separate application-only user.
+19. As an administrator, I want to reject a signup request and notify the applicant, so that unsuitable requests can be resolved and their submitted data removed.
+20. As an administrator, I want to select optional initial groups explicitly, so that new users receive only intended memberships.
+21. As an administrator, I want initial memberships to default to member, so that management authority is not granted accidentally.
+22. As an administrator, I want to select manager or owner roles explicitly when authorized, so that onboarding can establish the intended group responsibilities.
+23. As an administrator, I want to distinguish account creation, membership assignment, and account handover completion, so that I can finish partially completed onboarding correctly.
+24. As an administrator, I want failed provisioning to remain recoverable, so that temporary Google or database failures do not lose an accepted applicant's request.
+25. As an administrator, I want repeated approval or retry attempts not to create duplicate accounts, so that recovery is safe.
+26. As an administrator, I want an email collision never to attach an applicant to an existing account, so that an applicant cannot receive someone else's identity.
+27. As an administrator, I want unreviewed signup requests to expire after 30 days, so that the review queue does not retain obsolete applications indefinitely.
+28. As an administrator, I want successful applicant form data removed after provisioning and handover, so that only the minimal provisioning record remains.
+
+### Workspace user self-service
+
+29. As a Workspace user, I want to sign in with my managed Google identity, so that I do not need another password or application account.
+30. As a Workspace user, I want my displayed profile to come from Google Workspace, so that changes made through Google's tools are reflected rather than contradicted by an application copy.
+31. As a Workspace user, I want to see only my own permitted profile and request, so that other users' information remains private.
+32. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact email change, so that the organization can reach me at the right address.
+33. As a Workspace user, I want to verify a replacement contact email, so that an administrator can approve a reachable address.
+34. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact phone change, so that the organization can maintain accurate contact information.
+35. As a Workspace user, I want to see my pending profile change request separately from my current profile, so that I understand which values are proposed and which are already authoritative in Google.
+36. As a Workspace user, I want a newer submission to replace my one pending request, so that an administrator reviews my latest intended changes.
+37. As a Workspace user, I want an email outcome for my profile change request, so that I know whether the changes were accepted or rejected.
+38. As a Workspace user, I want rejection to leave my Google profile unchanged, so that unapproved proposals cannot alter my account.
+39. As a Workspace user, I want my application access to stop after my account is suspended or deleted, so that application sessions do not bypass Workspace account status.
+
+### Profile approval and permission enforcement
+
+40. As an administrator, I want to review pending profile change requests, so that contact changes can be approved without giving ordinary users Directory write authority.
+41. As an administrator, I want an email notification when a verified profile change request is submitted, so that I can respond without continuous polling.
+42. As an administrator, I want to approve or reject the entire reviewed request, so that the outcome is unambiguous.
+43. As an administrator, I want approval to apply only the request version I reviewed, so that a concurrent replacement cannot change what I authorize.
+44. As an administrator, I want approved changes to preserve unrelated Google contact entries and recovery settings, so that updating contact information does not damage other account data.
+45. As an administrator, I want management operations to execute under my Google OAuth credentials, so that Google enforces my privileges and resource restrictions.
+46. As an administrator, I want permission denials to be reported without escalation to another account, so that the application cannot bypass Google's authorization decisions.
+47. As an administrator, I want Google-side role changes to affect application permissions, so that the application does not retain stale administrator authority.
+
+### User administration and offboarding
+
+48. As an administrator, I want to list Workspace users within my authorized scope, so that I can find the accounts I manage.
+49. As an administrator, I want to view and edit Google-supported user information within my privileges, so that I can manage fields that ordinary users cannot change.
+50. As an administrator, I want to suspend a Workspace user, so that I can stop access while retaining the account and its data.
+51. As an administrator, I want to unsuspend a Workspace user when authorized, so that reversible offboarding can be undone.
+52. As an administrator, I want deletion to be a distinct, explicitly confirmed action after data disposition, so that permanent removal does not happen accidentally or before the organization has dealt with the user's data.
+
+### Group administration
+
+53. As an administrator, I want to list Google Groups, so that I can find the groups I am authorized to manage.
+54. As an administrator, I want to create a group and edit its basic details, so that the organization's group structure stays useful.
+55. As an administrator, I want to delete a group when authorized, so that obsolete groups can be removed.
+56. As an administrator, I want to inspect direct group memberships, so that I can understand who belongs to each group and in which role.
+57. As an administrator, I want to add or remove direct Workspace-user memberships, so that group access and mailing-list membership match organizational needs.
+58. As an administrator, I want to assign and change member, manager, and owner roles, so that group responsibilities are managed explicitly.
+59. As an administrator, I want unrelated existing group settings preserved, so that basic management does not unexpectedly change posting or privacy behavior.
+60. As an organization operator, I want group owner/manager roles and notification-group membership not to grant application-wide administrator authority, so that authorization remains tied to Google administrative privileges.
+
+### Operations, privacy, and usability
+
+61. As an organization operator, I want emails sent through a dedicated Workspace mailbox, so that notifications use an organization-controlled identity with send-only permission.
+62. As an organization operator, I want review notifications delivered to one configured Google Group, so that recipients can be managed through Google without an application role system.
+63. As an organization operator, I want notification emails to contain minimal personal information and a review link, so that submitted profiles and secrets are not distributed unnecessarily.
+64. As an organization operator, I want email failures to be visible and safely retryable, so that requests and outcomes do not disappear silently.
+65. As an organization operator, I want OAuth connections to report revocation or reconnection needs, so that failed credentials can be repaired without silently changing the acting identity.
+66. As an organization operator, I want workflow records separated from Google-authoritative profiles, so that the application does not create a second directory or permission system.
+67. As an organization operator, I want serverless hosting and a database that can become idle, so that a small workload has low ongoing cost.
+68. As an organization operator, I want provider tier management handled manually, so that the application does not introduce billing features or automatic upgrades.
+69. As an organization operator, I want public submissions and verification emails protected against invalid input and abuse, so that avoidable misuse does not consume limited resources.
+70. As an applicant or Workspace user, I want accessible forms and clear loading, success, and error states, so that I can complete workflows using the existing consistent UI.
+
+## Implementation Decisions
+
+### Domain and module interfaces
+
+- Preserve the agreed vocabulary: applicant, signup request, Workspace user, administrator, contact email, Workspace email, profile change request, account handover, suspension, deletion, group, group membership, group manager, group owner, and initial group membership.
+- Support one Workspace organization. A personal Google account used elsewhere is not the applicant's new managed identity.
+- Extend the existing application with public signup, own-profile self-service, administrator review, user administration, and group administration. Expose their behavior through the running application's browser-facing interface rather than inventing a separate public management API.
+- Keep request handling, authorization, persistence, and Google operations behind that application interface. Reuse existing patterns and installed dependencies; do not create one-to-one pass-through modules or speculative abstractions.
+- Trust-boundary contracts validate inputs, authenticated identity, ownership, current authority, request version, and completion state on the server. Browser-provided identifiers never establish ownership or privileges.
+
+### Identity and Google access
+
+- Existing Workspace users authenticate through Google. Validate token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and applicable state/nonce protections; enforce organizational membership from verified identity claims, not an email suffix or sign-in UI hint.
+- Bind the authenticated identity to a stable Google Directory user identifier server-side. Handle primary-email changes safely. Do not assume undocumented equality between the OpenID Connect subject and the Directory user identifier.
+- Re-evaluate account status for protected access so suspension or deletion cannot be bypassed by a previously issued application session. Google-side privilege changes must also be respected.
+- Ordinary-user consent does not authorize Directory writes. Self-service therefore submits approval requests rather than writing directly to Google.
+- Use the acting administrator's OAuth connection for administrative reads and writes. Google enforces that account's action, resource, and organizational-unit restrictions. Do not use a stronger shared writer, infer authority from broad administrator flags alone, or retry a denial under another identity.
+- Request the user-management and group-management Directory scopes required by the selected operations. Add read-only role inspection only when the interface needs it and the calling account is authorized. If roles are interpreted, account for indirect assignments, privilege hierarchy, and assignment scope.
+- Ordinary-user Directory reads expose domain-public information and do not document a full own-profile exception. Provide private own-profile display through an isolated backend OAuth reader with the Directory user read-only scope and a delegated account limited to Users Read in relevant organizational units. Derive the target from the authenticated session and return only permitted own-profile fields. This reader performs no writes and does not expand administrator listings beyond the acting administrator's scope.
+- Keep reader, acting-administrator, and notification-sender grants isolated by purpose, including protection against accidentally accumulating write grants on the reader. Credentials remain server-side and protected; revoked or expired connections have explicit reconnection behavior.
+- Do not use domain-wide delegation initially. This avoids its broad impersonation authority while accepting administrator approval delays for contact changes.
+
+### Signup, approval, and account handover
+
+- Require given name, family name, and verified contact email; phone is optional. Email verification precedes entry into the review queue. There is no applicant login/dashboard.
+- Generate Workspace email suggestions using the agreed given.family convention. The reviewing administrator confirms or edits them; applicants have no address-selection interface. Validate suggestions against Google naming rules and availability without connecting a collision to an existing user.
+- Acceptance provisions through Google under the approving administrator's authority. Initial group memberships are optional and explicit, with member as the default and manager/owner as deliberate selections.
+- Generate a random temporary password only for the Google creation operation, require a password change, and do not retain or expose that password in workflow records, logs, or emails.
+- Account handover remains a manual Google Admin console operation: reset the existing user's password with required change enabled and email Google's reset link to an address the applicant can access. Track handover completion before purging successful applicant form data.
+- Distinguish account creation, initial membership completion, and account handover so failures can be recovered without repeating completed work or creating another account.
+- Reject stale or already-resolved review actions. Preserve sufficient progress to recover when an external operation succeeds but later database or notification work fails; do not claim a distributed atomic transaction across Google and Postgres.
+- Rejected requests are deleted after outcome notification. Unreviewed signup requests expire after 30 days. Successful applicant form data is removed after provisioning and handover; retain only a minimal provisioning record identifying the Google account and approving administrator.
+
+### Profile change requests
+
+- Users may propose contact email and phone changes only. Name, Workspace email, organizational assignments, memberships, account status, recovery fields, and security settings remain administrator-controlled.
+- Store proposals separately from the current Google profile. Verify a replacement contact email before approval; replacing it requires verification of the new proposal.
+- Allow at most one pending profile change request per Workspace user. A new submission replaces it. Enforce this constraint in persistence, not just the interface.
+- Approval/rejection applies to the whole reviewed request. Use request-version/concurrency protection so a replaced proposal cannot be approved with stale reviewed contents.
+- Approved values are written with the approving administrator's OAuth credentials. Contact email and phone belong in Google contact arrays, not the Workspace primary address or account-recovery fields.
+- Preserve unrelated contact-array entries when submitting complete desired arrays to Google. Show success only after the relevant Google write succeeds; rejection leaves the profile unchanged.
+- Notification failure after a successful write must not cause the write to be repeated as if it had failed.
+
+### User and group administration
+
+- Provide authorized user listing, profile editing, suspension, unsuspension, and deletion. Permission checks apply to each action and target, not merely access to an administrator screen.
+- Suspension is the standard offboarding action. Deletion requires distinct confirmation that data disposition has been resolved manually in Google's Admin console. Do not implement automated data transfer.
+- Provide basic Google Group listing, creation, detail editing, and deletion, plus direct membership inspection, addition, removal, and member/manager/owner role changes for Workspace users.
+- Preserve unrelated existing group settings. Group owner/manager roles do not automatically confer application administrator authority.
+- Paginate Google lists correctly. Treat Google permissions, propagation delays, resource conflicts, and missing records as actual external outcomes rather than silently bypassing them.
+
+### Persistence and recovery
+
+- Use Drizzle ORM with Neon Postgres for signup requests, email-verification evidence, pending profile change requests, workflow progress/versioning, minimal provisioning records, and necessary protected OAuth/session state.
+- Store only the fields and constraints required by those workflows: verified-contact binding, stable Google identifiers, expiry timestamps, request versions, completion/progress state, and notification retry state where needed.
+- Do not maintain an authoritative local copy of existing user profiles, group memberships, or administrator roles. Verification evidence does not make the application's contact value authoritative over Google.
+- Make review actions, cleanup, notification retries, and provisioning recovery safe under concurrent or repeated execution.
+- Enforce expiration when requests are viewed or acted on. Daily cleanup is sufficient for eventual removal; it must tolerate missed or duplicate scheduling rather than relying on an exact invocation time.
+- Accept Neon's native Free recovery initially, including its currently documented six-hour restore window for application-owned records. Independent backups are deferred; Google remains authoritative for managed Workspace data.
+
+### Email, UI, and deployment
+
+- Send verification, outcome, and administrator-notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with an offline OAuth grant limited to Gmail send permission and no Directory administrator privileges.
+- Send administrator notifications for verified signup and profile change submissions to one configured Google Group. Include a review-queue link and minimal personal information, never passwords, verification secrets, or full submitted profiles.
+- Notification-group membership controls delivery only. Configure posting permission and recipient subscriptions so the selected mailbox can reach reviewers; notification links still require authenticated, authorized review access.
+- Make email delivery failures visible and retryable without losing requests or repeating completed Google operations. Protect verification tokens and rate-limit public submissions and verification sending.
+- Use the existing preconfigured shadcn/Tailwind UI and accessible native form behavior. Include explicit pending, empty, denied, success, and failure states where the workflow requires them; no manually authored UI CSS.
+- Deploy the existing Next.js application on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres. Prefer serverless/on-demand execution and database scale-to-zero; avoid continuous polling and always-on infrastructure.
+- Provider plan selection, tier changes, and allowances are handled manually. Do not implement tier management, quota-based upgrades, or application billing.
+
+## Testing Decisions
+
+- **Approved primary seam:** the running application's browser-facing interface. Exercise real screens, server operations, validation, sessions, authorization, workflow transitions, and persistence through that interface. Keep one primary application-level seam rather than separate helper or UI-structure suites.
+- **Good tests assert external behavior:** what an actor can see or do, what request state is persisted, whether a Google operation occurs under the correct identity, and what notification is sent. Do not assert internal function calls, private module arrangement, component markup structure, or implementation-specific timing.
+- **Modules exercised:** the application module spanning signup, verification, identity/access, own-profile display, profile proposals, administrator review, user administration, group administration, account handover tracking, expiry, notification delivery, and recovery. Test these through their shared application interface, not individually invented testing interfaces.
+- **Database:** use an isolated real Postgres database with the actual Drizzle schema/migrations, so uniqueness, request replacement, concurrent approval, progress persistence, and cleanup are tested against real database behavior. Tests must not use production workflow records.
+- **External adapters:** control Google identity/OAuth, Directory, and Gmail responses at their external interfaces. Simulate permission denials, revoked credentials, propagation delay, conflicting/missing resources, successful writes followed by later failures, and notification failure. Keep production authentication and authorization enforcement active rather than adding bypasses solely for tests.
+- **Identity/privacy checks:** cover invalid or wrong-organization identities, arbitrary target identifiers, another user's request/profile access, private own-profile reads through the read-only connection, administrator scope restrictions, role revocation, suspension, and deletion while an application session exists.
+- **Signup checks:** cover required fields, email verification, absence of applicant email choice, programmatic suggestions and conflicts, acceptance/rejection, optional role-specific memberships, handover tracking, 30-day expiry, data removal, concurrent approval, and recovery without duplicate creation.
+- **Profile checks:** cover proposed versus authoritative values, replacement-email verification, one pending request, replacement during review, whole-request decisions, permission denial, unchanged Google data on rejection, preservation of unrelated contact/recovery fields, and retry after notification failure without repeating a completed write.
+- **Administration checks:** cover authorized user editing, suspend/unsuspend, deletion confirmation/data-disposition prerequisite, group creation/edit/deletion, and direct member/manager/owner changes. Ensure group roles and notification-group membership do not become application-wide permissions.
+- **Notification/retention checks:** assert verified submission notifications, minimal email contents, protected review links, outcomes, recoverable sending failures, cleanup idempotency, expiry enforcement even when cleanup is delayed, and successful/rejected applicant-data removal at the agreed points.
+- **Live integration check:** perform a small controlled check in the actual Workspace organization for delegated-admin creation authority, role/OU restrictions, private profile reads, member/manager/owner support, OAuth reconnection, and notification-group delivery. Verify the manual Google reset-email handover. Simulated Google responses cannot establish these tenant capabilities; use dedicated test accounts/resources for destructive checks.
+- **Prior art:** the repository has no application tests, configured test runner, or existing workflow seams to reuse. Reuse the real Next.js application interface and existing Drizzle/Neon setup; select only the minimal browser-test tooling needed to make these checks runnable.
+- **Required checks:** run the repository lint, formatting, and build checks alongside the meaningful workflow/authorization checks. Add lower-level tests only if a demonstrated behavior cannot be reliably covered through the approved seam.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Multiple independent Workspace organizations or a multi-tenant product.
+- Applicant Google login, applicant dashboards, or applicant-selected Workspace addresses.
+- Immediate ordinary-user Directory writes without administrator approval.
+- Application-owned administrator roles, duplicated authoritative profiles/memberships, shared stronger write credentials, or domain-wide delegation.
+- User self-service changes to names, Workspace email, organizational assignments, group memberships, account status, recovery fields, or security settings.
+- Automatic initial group memberships or implicit grants of owner/manager authority.
+- Nested-group management, external-member management, and a group posting/privacy settings editor.
+- Automated data transfer, automated password-reset-link generation through undocumented APIs, plaintext-password delivery, or fully automated account handover.
+- Notifications that expose full submitted profiles or make their recipients authorized reviewers by membership alone.
+- Provider tier management, automatic paid upgrades, billing features, always-on workers, or continuous review-queue polling.
+- Independent backups beyond the accepted Neon native recovery initially.
+- Speculative abstractions, a separate public management API, exhaustive per-helper tests, or a UI redesign that replaces the configured shadcn system.
+
+## Further Notes
+
+- The owner approved the product decisions and the proposed primary testing seam. This specification synthesizes that agreement rather than reopening product questions.
+- This issue is the canonical implementation specification. Preserve the agreed glossary and architectural rationale during implementation, and follow the repository worktree/stacked-PR workflow and installed Next.js documentation before writing framework code.
+- **Delegated-admin creation remains an integration check:** current Google documentation conflicts about creating users through the Directory API as a delegated administrator. Verify the intended role in the actual tenant before relying on it. If Google denies creation, an appropriately privileged administrator must perform the approval; never escalate silently.
+- **Group manager support:** validate Groups for Business availability and actual member/manager/owner behavior in the tenant.
+- **Recovery and cost:** Google-managed data and local pending workflow records have different recovery characteristics. The organization accepts native Neon recovery initially and manages provider tiers manually; free allowances are not an unlimited-operation guarantee.
+- **Manual handover is intentional:** Google account creation and the Admin console reset-email procedure are separate steps. Track the latter rather than declaring onboarding fully complete immediately after account creation.
+- Official references: [Directory users and non-admin access](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/manage-users), [Directory read views](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/get), [user creation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/insert), [user update semantics](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/update), [administrator privileges](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/administrator-privilege-definitions), [delegation trade-offs](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/domain-wide-delegation-best-practices), [Console password-reset handover](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/reset-a-users-password), [Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), and [Neon plans](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans).
