19. As an administrator, I want to reject a signup request and notify the applicant, so that unsuitable requests can be resolved and their submitted data removed.
20. As an administrator, I want to select optional initial groups explicitly, so that new users receive only intended memberships.
21. As an administrator, I want initial memberships to default to member, so that management authority is not granted accidentally.
22. As an administrator, I want to select manager or owner roles explicitly when authorized, so that onboarding can establish the intended group responsibilities.
23. As an administrator, I want to distinguish account creation, membership assignment, and account handover completion, so that I can finish partially completed onboarding correctly.
24. As an administrator, I want failed provisioning to remain recoverable, so that temporary Google or database failures do not lose an accepted applicant's request.
25. As an administrator, I want repeated approval or retry attempts not to create duplicate accounts, so that recovery is safe.
26. As an administrator, I want an email collision never to attach an applicant to an existing account, so that an applicant cannot receive someone else's identity.
27. As an administrator, I want unreviewed signup requests to expire after 30 days, so that the review queue does not retain obsolete applications indefinitely.
28. As an administrator, I want successful applicant form data removed after provisioning and handover, so that only the minimal provisioning record remains.

### Workspace user self-service

29. As a Workspace user, I want to sign in with my managed Google identity, so that I do not need another password or application account.
30. As a Workspace user, I want my displayed profile to come from Google Workspace, so that changes made through Google's tools are reflected rather than contradicted by an application copy.
31. As a Workspace user, I want to see only my own permitted profile and request, so that other users' information remains private.
32. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact email change, so that the organization can reach me at the right address.
33. As a Workspace user, I want to verify a replacement contact email, so that an administrator can approve a reachable address.
34. As a Workspace user, I want to propose a contact phone change, so that the organization can maintain accurate contact information.
35. As a Workspace user, I want to see my pending profile change request separately from my current profile, so that I understand which values are proposed and which are already authoritative in Google.
36. As a Workspace user, I want a newer submission to replace my one pending request, so that an administrator reviews my latest intended changes.
37. As a Workspace user, I want an email outcome for my profile change request, so that I know whether the changes were accepted or rejected.
38. As a Workspace user, I want rejection to leave my Google profile unchanged, so that unapproved proposals cannot alter my account.
39. As a Workspace user, I want my application access to stop after my account is suspended or deleted, so that application sessions do not bypass Workspace account status.

### Profile approval and permission enforcement

40. As an administrator, I want to review pending profile change requests, so that contact changes can be approved without giving ordinary users Directory write authority.
41. As an administrator, I want an email notification when a verified profile change request is submitted, so that I can respond without continuous polling.
42. As an administrator, I want to approve or reject the entire reviewed request, so that the outcome is unambiguous.
43. As an administrator, I want approval to apply only the request version I reviewed, so that a concurrent replacement cannot change what I authorize.
44. As an administrator, I want approved changes to preserve unrelated Google contact entries and recovery settings, so that updating contact information does not damage other account data.
45. As an administrator, I want management operations to execute under my Google OAuth credentials, so that Google enforces my privileges and resource restrictions.
46. As an administrator, I want permission denials to be reported without escalation to another account, so that the application cannot bypass Google's authorization decisions.
47. As an administrator, I want Google-side role changes to affect application permissions, so that the application does not retain stale administrator authority.

### User administration and offboarding

48. As an administrator, I want to list Workspace users within my authorized scope, so that I can find the accounts I manage.
49. As an administrator, I want to view and edit Google-supported user information within my privileges, so that I can manage fields that ordinary users cannot change.
50. As an administrator, I want to suspend a Workspace user, so that I can stop access while retaining the account and its data.
51. As an administrator, I want to unsuspend a Workspace user when authorized, so that reversible offboarding can be undone.
52. As an administrator, I want deletion to be a distinct, explicitly confirmed action after data disposition, so that permanent removal does not happen accidentally or before the organization has dealt with the user's data.

### Group administration

53. As an administrator, I want to list Google Groups, so that I can find the groups I am authorized to manage.
54. As an administrator, I want to create a group and edit its basic details, so that the organization's group structure stays useful.
55. As an administrator, I want to delete a group when authorized, so that obsolete groups can be removed.
56. As an administrator, I want to inspect direct group memberships, so that I can understand who belongs to each group and in which role.
57. As an administrator, I want to add or remove direct Workspace-user memberships, so that group access and mailing-list membership match organizational needs.
58. As an administrator, I want to assign and change member, manager, and owner roles, so that group responsibilities are managed explicitly.
59. As an administrator, I want unrelated existing group settings preserved, so that basic management does not unexpectedly change posting or privacy behavior.
60. As an organization operator, I want group owner/manager roles and notification-group membership not to grant application-wide administrator authority, so that authorization remains tied to Google administrative privileges.

### Operations, privacy, and usability

61. As an organization operator, I want emails sent through a dedicated Workspace mailbox, so that notifications use an organization-controlled identity with send-only permission.
62. As an organization operator, I want review notifications delivered to one configured Google Group, so that recipients can be managed through Google without an application role system.
63. As an organization operator, I want notification emails to contain minimal personal information and a review link, so that submitted profiles and secrets are not distributed unnecessarily.
64. As an organization operator, I want email failures to be visible and safely retryable, so that requests and outcomes do not disappear silently.
65. As an organization operator, I want OAuth connections to report revocation or reconnection needs, so that failed credentials can be repaired without silently changing the acting identity.
66. As an organization operator, I want workflow records separated from Google-authoritative profiles, so that the application does not create a second directory or permission system.
67. As an organization operator, I want serverless hosting and a database that can become idle, so that a small workload has low ongoing cost.
68. As an organization operator, I want provider tier management handled manually, so that the application does not introduce billing features or automatic upgrades.
69. As an organization operator, I want public submissions and verification emails protected against invalid input and abuse, so that avoidable misuse does not consume limited resources.
70. As an applicant or Workspace user, I want accessible forms and clear loading, success, and error states, so that I can complete workflows using the existing consistent UI.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain and module interfaces

- Preserve the agreed vocabulary: applicant, signup request, Workspace user, administrator, contact email, Workspace email, profile change request, account handover, suspension, deletion, group, group membership, group manager, group owner, and initial group membership.
- Support one Workspace organization. A personal Google account used elsewhere is not the applicant's new managed identity.
- Extend the existing application with public signup, own-profile self-service, administrator review, user administration, and group administration. Expose their behavior through the running application's browser-facing interface rather than inventing a separate public management API.
- Keep request handling, authorization, persistence, and Google operations behind that application interface. Reuse existing patterns and installed dependencies; do not create one-to-one pass-through modules or speculative abstractions.
- Trust-boundary contracts validate inputs, authenticated identity, ownership, current authority, request version, and completion state on the server. Browser-provided identifiers never establish ownership or privileges.

### Identity and Google access

- Existing Workspace users authenticate through Google. Validate token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and applicable state/nonce protections; enforce organizational membership from verified identity claims, not an email suffix or sign-in UI hint.
- Bind the authenticated identity to a stable Google Directory user identifier server-side. Handle primary-email changes safely. Do not assume undocumented equality between the OpenID Connect subject and the Directory user identifier.
- Re-evaluate account status for protected access so suspension or deletion cannot be bypassed by a previously issued application session. Google-side privilege changes must also be respected.
- Ordinary-user consent does not authorize Directory writes. Self-service therefore submits approval requests rather than writing directly to Google.
- Use the acting administrator's OAuth connection for administrative reads and writes. Google enforces that account's action, resource, and organizational-unit restrictions. Do not use a stronger shared writer, infer authority from broad administrator flags alone, or retry a denial under another identity.
- Request the user-management and group-management Directory scopes required by the selected operations. Add read-only role inspection only when the interface needs it and the calling account is authorized. If roles are interpreted, account for indirect assignments, privilege hierarchy, and assignment scope.
- Ordinary-user Directory reads expose domain-public information and do not document a full own-profile exception. Provide private own-profile display through an isolated backend OAuth reader with the Directory user read-only scope and a delegated account limited to Users Read in relevant organizational units. Derive the target from the authenticated session and return only permitted own-profile fields. This reader performs no writes and does not expand administrator listings beyond the acting administrator's scope.
- Keep reader, acting-administrator, and notification-sender grants isolated by purpose, including protection against accidentally accumulating write grants on the reader. Credentials remain server-side and protected; revoked or expired connections have explicit reconnection behavior.
- Do not use domain-wide delegation initially. This avoids its broad impersonation authority while accepting administrator approval delays for contact changes.

### Signup, approval, and account handover

- Require given name, family name, and verified contact email; phone is optional. Email verification precedes entry into the review queue. There is no applicant login/dashboard.
- Generate Workspace email suggestions using the agreed given.family convention. The reviewing administrator confirms or edits them; applicants have no address-selection interface. Validate suggestions against Google naming rules and availability without connecting a collision to an existing user.
- Acceptance provisions through Google under the approving administrator's authority. Initial group memberships are optional and explicit, with member as the default and manager/owner as deliberate selections.
- Generate a random temporary password only for the Google creation operation, require a password change, and do not retain or expose that password in workflow records, logs, or emails.
- Account handover remains a manual Google Admin console operation: reset the existing user's password with required change enabled and email Google's reset link to an address the applicant can access. Track handover completion before purging successful applicant form data.
- Distinguish account creation, initial membership completion, and account handover so failures can be recovered without repeating completed work or creating another account.
- Reject stale or already-resolved review actions. Preserve sufficient progress to recover when an external operation succeeds but later database or notification work fails; do not claim a distributed atomic transaction across Google and Postgres.
- Rejected requests are deleted after outcome notification. Unreviewed signup requests expire after 30 days. Successful applicant form data is removed after provisioning and handover; retain only a minimal provisioning record identifying the Google account and approving administrator.

### Profile change requests

- Users may propose contact email and phone changes only. Name, Workspace email, organizational assignments, memberships, account status, recovery fields, and security settings remain administrator-controlled.
- Store proposals separately from the current Google profile. Verify a replacement contact email before approval; replacing it requires verification of the new proposal.
- Allow at most one pending profile change request per Workspace user. A new submission replaces it. Enforce this constraint in persistence, not just the interface.
- Approval/rejection applies to the whole reviewed request. Use request-version/concurrency protection so a replaced proposal cannot be approved with stale reviewed contents.
- Approved values are written with the approving administrator's OAuth credentials. Contact email and phone belong in Google contact arrays, not the Workspace primary address or account-recovery fields.
- Preserve unrelated contact-array entries when submitting complete desired arrays to Google. Show success only after the relevant Google write succeeds; rejection leaves the profile unchanged.
- Notification failure after a successful write must not cause the write to be repeated as if it had failed.

### User and group administration

- Provide authorized user listing, profile editing, suspension, unsuspension, and deletion. Permission checks apply to each action and target, not merely access to an administrator screen.
- Suspension is the standard offboarding action. Deletion requires distinct confirmation that data disposition has been resolved manually in Google's Admin console. Do not implement automated data transfer.
- Provide basic Google Group listing, creation, detail editing, and deletion, plus direct membership inspection, addition, removal, and member/manager/owner role changes for Workspace users.
- Preserve unrelated existing group settings. Group owner/manager roles do not automatically confer application administrator authority.
- Paginate Google lists correctly. Treat Google permissions, propagation delays, resource conflicts, and missing records as actual external outcomes rather than silently bypassing them.

### Persistence and recovery

- Use Drizzle ORM with Neon Postgres for signup requests, email-verification evidence, pending profile change requests, workflow progress/versioning, minimal provisioning records, and necessary protected OAuth/session state.
- Store only the fields and constraints required by those workflows: verified-contact binding, stable Google identifiers, expiry timestamps, request versions, completion/progress state, and notification retry state where needed.
- Do not maintain an authoritative local copy of existing user profiles, group memberships, or administrator roles. Verification evidence does not make the application's contact value authoritative over Google.
- Make review actions, cleanup, notification retries, and provisioning recovery safe under concurrent or repeated execution.
- Enforce expiration when requests are viewed or acted on. Daily cleanup is sufficient for eventual removal; it must tolerate missed or duplicate scheduling rather than relying on an exact invocation time.
- Accept Neon's native Free recovery initially, including its currently documented six-hour restore window for application-owned records. Independent backups are deferred; Google remains authoritative for managed Workspace data.

### Email, UI, and deployment

- Send verification, outcome, and administrator-notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with an offline OAuth grant limited to Gmail send permission and no Directory administrator privileges.
- Send administrator notifications for verified signup and profile change submissions to one configured Google Group. Include a review-queue link and minimal personal information, never passwords, verification secrets, or full submitted profiles.
- Notification-group membership controls delivery only. Configure posting permission and recipient subscriptions so the selected mailbox can reach reviewers; notification links still require authenticated, authorized review access.
- Make email delivery failures visible and retryable without losing requests or repeating completed Google operations. Protect verification tokens and rate-limit public submissions and verification sending.
- Use the existing preconfigured shadcn/Tailwind UI and accessible native form behavior. Include explicit pending, empty, denied, success, and failure states where the workflow requires them; no manually authored UI CSS.
- Deploy the existing Next.js application on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres. Prefer serverless/on-demand execution and database scale-to-zero; avoid continuous polling and always-on infrastructure.
- Provider plan selection, tier changes, and allowances are handled manually. Do not implement tier management, quota-based upgrades, or application billing.

## Testing Decisions

- **Approved primary seam:** the running application's browser-facing interface. Exercise real screens, server operations, validation, sessions, authorization, workflow transitions, and persistence through that interface. Keep one primary application-level seam rather than separate helper or UI-structure suites.
- **Good tests assert external behavior:** what an actor can see or do, what request state is persisted, whether a Google operation occurs under the correct identity, and what notification is sent. Do not assert internal function calls, private module arrangement, component markup structure, or implementation-specific timing.
- **Modules exercised:** the application module spanning signup, verification, identity/access, own-profile display, profile proposals, administrator review, user administration, group administration, account handover tracking, expiry, notification delivery, and recovery. Test these through their shared application interface, not individually invented testing interfaces.
- **Database:** use an isolated real Postgres database with the actual Drizzle schema/migrations, so uniqueness, request replacement, concurrent approval, progress persistence, and cleanup are tested against real database behavior. Tests must not use production workflow records.
- **External adapters:** control Google identity/OAuth, Directory, and Gmail responses at their external interfaces. Simulate permission denials, revoked credentials, propagation delay, conflicting/missing resources, successful writes followed by later failures, and notification failure. Keep production authentication and authorization enforcement active rather than adding bypasses solely for tests.
- **Identity/privacy checks:** cover invalid or wrong-organization identities, arbitrary target identifiers, another user's request/profile access, private own-profile reads through the read-only connection, administrator scope restrictions, role revocation, suspension, and deletion while an application session exists.
- **Signup checks:** cover required fields, email verification, absence of applicant email choice, programmatic suggestions and conflicts, acceptance/rejection, optional role-specific memberships, handover tracking, 30-day expiry, data removal, concurrent approval, and recovery without duplicate creation.
- **Profile checks:** cover proposed versus authoritative values, replacement-email verification, one pending request, replacement during review, whole-request decisions, permission denial, unchanged Google data on rejection, preservation of unrelated contact/recovery fields, and retry after notification failure without repeating a completed write.
- **Administration checks:** cover authorized user editing, suspend/unsuspend, deletion confirmation/data-disposition prerequisite, group creation/edit/deletion, and direct member/manager/owner changes. Ensure group roles and notification-group membership do not become application-wide permissions.
- **Notification/retention checks:** assert verified submission notifications, minimal email contents, protected review links, outcomes, recoverable sending failures, cleanup idempotency, expiry enforcement even when cleanup is delayed, and successful/rejected applicant-data removal at the agreed points.
- **Live integration check:** perform a small controlled check in the actual Workspace organization for delegated-admin creation authority, role/OU restrictions, private profile reads, member/manager/owner support, OAuth reconnection, and notification-group delivery. Verify the manual Google reset-email handover. Simulated Google responses cannot establish these tenant capabilities; use dedicated test accounts/resources for destructive checks.
- **Prior art:** the repository has no application tests, configured test runner, or existing workflow seams to reuse. Reuse the real Next.js application interface and existing Drizzle/Neon setup; select only the minimal browser-test tooling needed to make these checks runnable.
- **Required checks:** run the repository lint, formatting, and build checks alongside the meaningful workflow/authorization checks. Add lower-level tests only if a demonstrated behavior cannot be reliably covered through the approved seam.

## Out of Scope

- Multiple independent Workspace organizations or a multi-tenant product.
- Applicant Google login, applicant dashboards, or applicant-selected Workspace addresses.
- Immediate ordinary-user Directory writes without administrator approval.
- Application-owned administrator roles, duplicated authoritative profiles/memberships, shared stronger write credentials, or domain-wide delegation.
- User self-service changes to names, Workspace email, organizational assignments, group memberships, account status, recovery fields, or security settings.
- Automatic initial group memberships or implicit grants of owner/manager authority.
- Nested-group management, external-member management, and a group posting/privacy settings editor.
- Automated data transfer, automated password-reset-link generation through undocumented APIs, plaintext-password delivery, or fully automated account handover.
- Notifications that expose full submitted profiles or make their recipients authorized reviewers by membership alone.
- Provider tier management, automatic paid upgrades, billing features, always-on workers, or continuous review-queue polling.
- Independent backups beyond the accepted Neon native recovery initially.
- Speculative abstractions, a separate public management API, exhaustive per-helper tests, or a UI redesign that replaces the configured shadcn system.

## Further Notes

- The owner approved the product decisions and the proposed primary testing seam. This specification synthesizes that agreement rather than reopening product questions.
- This issue is the canonical implementation specification. Preserve the agreed glossary and architectural rationale during implementation, and follow the repository worktree/stacked-PR workflow and installed Next.js documentation before writing framework code.
- **Delegated-admin creation remains an integration check:** current Google documentation conflicts about creating users through the Directory API as a delegated administrator. Verify the intended role in the actual tenant before relying on it. If Google denies creation, an appropriately privileged administrator must perform the approval; never escalate silently.
- **Group manager support:** validate Groups for Business availability and actual member/manager/owner behavior in the tenant.
- **Recovery and cost:** Google-managed data and local pending workflow records have different recovery characteristics. The organization accepts native Neon recovery initially and manages provider tiers manually; free allowances are not an unlimited-operation guarantee.
- **Manual handover is intentional:** Google account creation and the Admin console reset-email procedure are separate steps. Track the latter rather than declaring onboarding fully complete immediately after account creation.
- Official references: [Directory users and non-admin access](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/manage-users), [Directory read views](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/get), [user creation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/insert), [user update semantics](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/update), [administrator privileges](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/administrator-privilege-definitions), [delegation trade-offs](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/domain-wide-delegation-best-practices), [Console password-reset handover](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/reset-a-users-password), [Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), and [Neon plans](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans).

1: # Issue tracker: GitHub
2: 
3: Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.
4: 
5: ## Conventions
6: 
7: - **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
8: - **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
9: - **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10: - **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
11: - **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
12: - **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`
13: 
14: Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.
15: 
16: ## Pull requests as a triage surface
17: 
18: **PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_
19: 
20: When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:
21: 
22: - **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
23: - **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
24: - **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.
25: 
26: GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.
27: 
28: ## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"
29: 
30: Create a GitHub issue.
31: 
32: ## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"
33: 
34: Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.
35: 
36: ## Wayfinding operations
37: 
38: Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.
39: 
40: - **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
41: - **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
42: - **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
43: - **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
44: - **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
45: - **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

## Conventions

- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.

display.text:
# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

# Workspace User Management

The nonprofit's onboarding, self-service, and administration of its Google Workspace users and groups.

## Language

**Applicant**:
A person requesting a Workspace account who has not yet received one through onboarding.
_Avoid_: User, pending user

**Signup request**:
An applicant's submitted information awaiting an administrator's acceptance or rejection.
_Avoid_: Account, pending user

**Workspace user**:
A person with a managed Google account in the nonprofit's Workspace organization.
_Avoid_: Applicant

**Administrator**:
A Workspace user whose Google Workspace administrative privileges authorize the relevant management action.
_Avoid_: App administrator

**Contact email**:
An email address used to contact a person, distinct from their managed Workspace email address.

**Workspace email**:
The primary email address of a person's managed Google Workspace account.

**Self-service**:
A Workspace user's submission of changes to their own contact information for administrator approval.

**Profile change request**:
A Workspace user's proposed contact email or phone changes awaiting approval together by an administrator with sufficient privileges. Each user has at most one pending request; a new submission replaces it.
_Avoid_: Profile update

**Account handover**:
Delivery of first-login access to an approved applicant after their Workspace account has been created.

**Suspension**:
Reversible deactivation of a Workspace account that retains the account and its data.
_Avoid_: Deletion, deactivation

**Deletion**:
Removal of a Workspace account after the organization has resolved the disposition of its data.
_Avoid_: Suspension, deactivation

**Group**:
A Google Group within the nonprofit's Workspace organization.

**Group membership**:
A Workspace user's relationship to a group, with a member, manager, or owner role.

**Group manager**:
A group member with Google's manager role in that group; this role does not itself confer application administrator authority.

**Group owner**:
A group member with Google's owner role in that group; this role does not itself confer application administrator authority.

**Initial group membership**:
A group membership explicitly selected by the reviewing administrator during onboarding, with no automatic assignments. Its role is member unless manager or owner is explicitly selected.

1: # Use administrator OAuth and approved profile changes
2: 
3: Ordinary-user OAuth consent does not authorize Directory profile writes, even to the user's own account. For this small nonprofit, users submit verified contact email and phone changes for approval; the application executes approved changes and administrative operations using the acting administrator's OAuth credentials. Google therefore enforces that administrator's privileges and resource restrictions, without a shared stronger account or a parallel application role model.
4: 
5: Prefer this workflow over domain-wide delegation: Google's Directory user write scope is not limited to contact fields, and delegation scopes do not restrict which account a service account may impersonate. The trade-off is that contact changes wait for an authorized administrator instead of taking effect immediately. Domain-wide delegation can be reconsidered if that approval delay becomes unacceptable.
6: 
7: Request `admin.directory.user` for user management and `admin.directory.group` for group and membership management; add read-only role inspection only if required for the interface. Restrict profile change requests to contact email and phone, preserve unrelated Directory entries, and keep Workspace email, account recovery fields, and security settings outside that workflow. A new contact email must be verified before it can be approved. Do not retry denied operations using stronger credentials.
8: 
9: Send verification, outcome, and administrator notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with a separate offline OAuth grant limited to `gmail.send`. Notify a configured Google Group when a verified signup or profile change request is submitted, including a review-queue link and minimal personal information. The notification group's membership determines delivery only, never approval authority; configure it to accept mail from the sender.
10: 
11: Ordinary-user Directory reads expose only domain-public information, without a documented exception for a user's own private profile. To display the user's actual contact information, use a separate backend-only OAuth connection with `admin.directory.user.readonly` and a delegated account limited to Users Read in the relevant organizational units. Resolve the target from the authenticated identity and return only that user's permitted profile fields. Keep this reader isolated from write grants; it must not perform administrative or approved-profile writes.
12: 
13: References: [Directory user permissions](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/manage-users#retrieve_a_user_as_a_non-administrator), [Directory read views](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/reference/rest/v1/users/get), [OAuth scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/directory/v1/guides/authorizing), [domain-wide delegation guidance](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/domain-wide-delegation-best-practices), and [existing-user password reset](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/reset-a-users-password).

(End of file - total 13 lines)
</content>

Google therefore enforces that administrator's privileges and resource restrictions, without a shared stronger account or a parallel application role model.

Prefer this workflow over domain-wide delegation: Google's Directory user write scope is not limited to contact fields, and delegation scopes do not restrict which account a service account may impersonate. Domain-wide delegation can be reconsidered if that approval delay becomes unacceptable.

Request `admin.directory.user` for user management and `admin.directory.group` for group and membership management; add read-only role inspection only if required for the interface. Restrict profile change requests to contact email and phone, preserve unrelated Directory entries, and keep Workspace email, account recovery fields, and security settings outside that workflow. A new contact email must be verified before it can be approved. Do not retry denied operations using stronger credentials.

Send verification, outcome, and administrator notification emails through a dedicated Workspace mailbox with a separate offline OAuth grant limited to `gmail.send`. Notify a configured Google Group when a verified signup or profile change request is submitted, including a review-queue link and minimal personal information. The notification group's membership determines delivery only, never approval authority; configure it to accept mail from the sender.

Ordinary-user Directory reads expose only domain-public information, without a documented exception for a user's own private profile. To display the user's actual contact information, use a separate backend-only OAuth connection with `admin.directory.user.readonly` and a delegated account limited to Users Read in the relevant organizational units. Resolve the target from the authenticated identity and return only that user's permitted profile fields. Keep this reader isolated from write grants; it must not perform administrative or approved-profile writes.

Proposed breakdown for [spec #1](https://github.com/itsmeyaw/binden/issues/1): **23 slices—21 AFK and 2 HITL**.

Each AFK slice includes its working UI, server behavior, necessary persistence/Google operations, and browser-facing tests against real isolated Postgres. Authorization, privacy, concurrency, and recoverable failures belong in the relevant slice.

“Blocked by” numbers below refer to this proposed list. “Stories” refer to the numbered user stories in #1.

### Identity and user administration

1. **Sign in and view your own Workspace profile**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** None · **Stories:** 29–31, 39, 65–66, 70  
   Google sign-in, protected sessions, stable identity resolution, and private own-profile display through the isolated read-only connection. Deny wrong-organization identities, cross-user access, and suspended/deleted accounts.

2. **List Workspace users under the acting administrator’s authority**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 1 · **Stories:** 45–48, 65  
   Connect the administrator’s OAuth grant and provide paginated user listing. Respect Google privileges and organizational-unit restrictions, including revoked grants and changed authority.

3. **Edit administrator-controlled user information**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 2 · **Stories:** 45–47, 49  
   View and edit supported user fields through Google, preserving unrelated information and showing permission denials clearly.

4. **Suspend and unsuspend a Workspace user**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 2 · **Stories:** 39, 45–47, 50–51  
   Complete reversible offboarding through the administrator interface, including loss of application access for an existing suspended-user session.

5. **Delete a Workspace user after data-disposition confirmation**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 2 · **Stories:** 45–47, 52  
   Provide distinct deletion confirmation acknowledging manual data disposition in Google’s Admin console. Handle denied, missing, and already-deleted accounts.

### Signup and onboarding

6. **Submit and verify a signup request for administrator review**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 2 · **Stories:** 1–8, 13, 15, 27, 61, 64, 66, 69–70  
   Public form → dedicated-mailbox verification → persisted verified request → protected administrator queue and details. Include abuse protection, sending-failure recovery, and enforcement of the 30-day review deadline.

7. **Reject a signup request and remove its submitted data**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 6 · **Stories:** 9, 12, 19, 64

8. **Notify the review group about verified signup requests**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 6 · **Stories:** 14, 60–64  
   Deliver minimal review notifications with protected queue links. Surface and retry sending failures without granting review authority through group membership.

9. **Accept a signup request and provision its Workspace account**  
   **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 6 · **Stories:** 16–18, 23–26, 45–47

10. **Complete account handover and remove successful applicant data**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 9 · **Stories:** 9–11, 23–25, 28, 64  
    Guide the administrator through Google’s manual reset-email handover, record completion, deliver the application outcome, and remove applicant form data at the agreed completion point.

### Group administration

11. **List groups and inspect their direct memberships**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 1 · **Stories:** 45–47, 53, 56, 60, 65

12. **Create a Google Group**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 11 · **Stories:** 54, 59  
    Create a group from the administrator interface and show the Google-backed result, including validation and address-conflict handling.

13. **Edit a group’s basic details**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 11 · **Stories:** 54, 59  
    Update basic details while preserving unrelated posting and privacy settings.

14. **Delete a Google Group**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 11 · **Stories:** 55

    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 11 · **Stories:** 56–57, 60

    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 15 · **Stories:** 58, 60

17. **Select initial group memberships during onboarding**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 10, 16 · **Stories:** 20–25

18. **Request and review a contact phone change**  
    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 2, 6 · **Stories:** 31, 34–38, 40, 42–47, 64, 66, 70

    **Type:** AFK · **Blocked by:** 18 · **Stories:** 32–33, 35–38, 40, 42–44, 64, 69

    **Type:** HITL · **Blocked by:** 1 · **Stories:** 29–31, 39, 65, 67–68

23. **Verify the complete lifecycle against the actual Workspace organization**  
    **Type:** HITL · **Blocked by:** 2–22 · **Stories:** Integration verification across the preceding slices  
    Use controlled test accounts/groups to verify administrator and organizational-unit restrictions, delegated-admin creation behavior, group manager/owner support, notification-group delivery, OAuth reconnection, manual account handover, and offboarding. Record actual tenant capabilities and resolve integration failures without credential escalation.

# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

+  const labels = json('label', 'list', '--repo', repo, '--limit', '100', '--json', 'name');
+  if (!labels.some((label) => label.name === 'ready-for-human')) {
+    gh('label', 'create', 'ready-for-human', '--repo', repo, '--description', 'Fully specified, requires human implementation or live verification', '--color', 'D4C5F9');
+    console.log('Created canonical ready-for-human label.');
+  }
+  const existing = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(existing, slice);
+    assert(matches.length <= 1, `Duplicate matching issues for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    const body = bodyFor(slice, published);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    let issue;
+    if (matches.length) {
+      issue = matches[0];
+      assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), body.trim(), `Existing slice ${slice.n} differs; inspect before changing`);
+      assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label));
+      console.log(`Reusing slice ${slice.n}: ${issue.url}`);
+    } else {
+      const url = gh('issue', 'create', '--repo', repo, '--title', slice.title, '--body', body, '--label', 'enhancement', '--label', label);
+      const number = Number(url.split('/').at(-1));
+      assert(Number.isInteger(number) && number !== 1, `Unexpected created issue URL: ${url}`);
+      issue = { number, url };
+      console.log(`Created slice ${slice.n} (${slice.type ?? 'AFK'}): ${url}`);
+    }
+    const data = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}`);
+    issue.databaseId = data.id;
+    published.set(slice.n, issue);
+    if (slice.deps.length) {
+      const current = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+      for (const n of slice.deps) {
+        const blocker = published.get(n);
+        if (!current.some((value) => value.id === blocker.databaseId)) {
+          gh('api', '--method', 'POST', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`, '-F', `issue_id=${blocker.databaseId}`);
+        }
+      }
+      console.log(`  Native blockers: ${slice.deps.map((n) => `#${published.get(n).number}`).join(', ')}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed during publication');
+  console.log(`Published ${published.size} slices; parent #1 unchanged. Verification fingerprint: ${expected}`);
+}

+function verify(expected) {
+  assert(expected, 'Supply the baseline parent fingerprint');
+  const all = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(all, slice);
+    assert.equal(matches.length, 1, `Expected exactly one issue for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    published.set(slice.n, matches[0]);
+  }
+  let edges = 0;
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const issue = published.get(slice.n);
+    assert.equal(issue.state, 'OPEN', `Slice ${slice.n} is not open`);
+    assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), bodyFor(slice, published).trim(), `Slice ${slice.n} body mismatch`);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label), `Slice ${slice.n} triage mismatch`);
+    assert(!issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === (slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-agent' : 'ready-for-human')));
+    const deps = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+    assert.deepEqual(deps.map((value) => value.number).sort((a, b) => a - b), slice.deps.map((n) => published.get(n).number).sort((a, b) => a - b), `Slice ${slice.n} native dependency mismatch`);
+    edges += deps.length;
+    console.log(`Verified ${slice.n}. #${issue.number}: ${issue.title} [${label}]`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed');
+  console.log(`Verified ${published.size} open issues, 21 AFK + 2 HITL, ${edges} native dependency edges, exact template bodies, and unchanged parent #1.`);

+const issues = () => json('issue', 'list', '--repo', repo, '--state', 'all', '--limit', '100', '--json', 'number,title,body,labels,state,url');
+const findSlice = (all, slice) => all.filter((issue) => issue.title === slice.title && issue.body.includes(parentUrl));
+const bodyFor = (slice, published) => {
+  const type = slice.type ?? 'AFK';
+  const blockers = slice.deps.length
+    ? slice.deps.map((n) => `- ${published.get(n).url}`).join('\n')
+    : 'None - can start immediately';
+  const criteria = type === 'AFK' ? [...slice.criteria, ...standard] : slice.criteria;
+  return `## Parent\n\n${parentUrl}\n\n## What to build\n\n**Type:** ${type}  \n**User stories covered:** ${slice.stories} (parent #1).\n\n${slice.build}\n\n${type === 'HITL' ? 'Requires an organization operator for live credentials, configuration, or tenant verification. Preserve all parent privacy/authorization boundaries and use controlled test resources.' : 'Use the parent’s approved application-level testing seam and Google-authoritative domain model. This issue is a complete behavioral slice, not a separate schema, API, UI, or test layer.'}\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n${criteria.map((criterion) => `- [ ] ${criterion}`).join('\n')}\n\n## Blocked by\n\n${blockers}\n`;
+};
+
+function publish() {
+  const before = parent();
+  const expected = fingerprint(before);
+  console.log(`Parent baseline fingerprint: ${expected}`);
+  const labels = json('label', 'list', '--repo', repo, '--limit', '100', '--json', 'name');
+  if (!labels.some((label) => label.name === 'ready-for-human')) {
+    gh('label', 'create', 'ready-for-human', '--repo', repo, '--description', 'Fully specified, requires human implementation or live verification', '--color', 'D4C5F9');
+    console.log('Created canonical ready-for-human label.');
+  }
+  const existing = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(existing, slice);
+    assert(matches.length <= 1, `Duplicate matching issues for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    const body = bodyFor(slice, published);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    let issue;
+    if (matches.length) {
+      issue = matches[0];
+      assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), body.trim(), `Existing slice ${slice.n} differs; inspect before changing`);
+      assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label));
+      console.log(`Reusing slice ${slice.n}: ${issue.url}`);
+    } else {
+      const url = gh('issue', 'create', '--repo', repo, '--title', slice.title, '--body', body, '--label', 'enhancement', '--label', label);
+      const number = Number(url.split('/').at(-1));
+      assert(Number.isInteger(number) && number !== 1, `Unexpected created issue URL: ${url}`);
+      issue = { number, url };
+      console.log(`Created slice ${slice.n} (${slice.type ?? 'AFK'}): ${url}`);
+    }
+    const data = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}`);
+    issue.databaseId = data.id;
+    published.set(slice.n, issue);
+    if (slice.deps.length) {
+      const current = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+      for (const n of slice.deps) {
+        const blocker = published.get(n);
+        if (!current.some((value) => value.id === blocker.databaseId)) {
+          gh('api', '--method', 'POST', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`, '-F', `issue_id=${blocker.databaseId}`);
+        }
+      }
+      console.log(`  Native blockers: ${slice.deps.map((n) => `#${published.get(n).number}`).join(', ')}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed during publication');
+  console.log(`Published ${published.size} slices; parent #1 unchanged. Verification fingerprint: ${expected}`);
+}
+
+function verify(expected) {
+  assert(expected, 'Supply the baseline parent fingerprint');
+  const all = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(all, slice);
+    assert.equal(matches.length, 1, `Expected exactly one issue for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    published.set(slice.n, matches[0]);
+  }
+  let edges = 0;
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const issue = published.get(slice.n);
+    assert.equal(issue.state, 'OPEN', `Slice ${slice.n} is not open`);
+    assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), bodyFor(slice, published).trim(), `Slice ${slice.n} body mismatch`);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label), `Slice ${slice.n} triage mismatch`);
+    assert(!issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === (slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-agent' : 'ready-for-human')));
+    const deps = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+    assert.deepEqual(deps.map((value) => value.number).sort((a, b) => a - b), slice.deps.map((n) => published.get(n).number).sort((a, b) => a - b), `Slice ${slice.n} native dependency mismatch`);
+    edges += deps.length;
+    console.log(`Verified ${slice.n}. #${issue.number}: ${issue.title} [${label}]`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed');
+  console.log(`Verified ${published.size} open issues, 21 AFK + 2 HITL, ${edges} native dependency edges, exact template bodies, and unchanged parent #1.`);
+}
+
+if (process.argv[2] === 'publish') publish();
+else if (process.argv[2] === 'verify') verify(process.argv[3]);
+else throw new Error('Use publish or verify <parent-fingerprint>');

+  {
+    n: 20, title: 'Notify the review group about profile change requests', deps: [8, 18], stories: '41, 60–64',
+    build: 'Notify the configured review group when a current profile change request becomes reviewable. Reuse the dedicated sender and delivery recovery behavior from signup notifications, with a protected link to the current profile request.',
+    criteria: [
+      'A reviewable current profile change request triggers a minimal notification through the dedicated Gmail send-only connection to the configured Google Group.',
+      'Phone-only submissions from verified Workspace sessions are reviewable immediately; any proposal containing a replacement email is not notified until its current email/request verification is complete.',
+      'Replacement/version handling prevents a stale verification event from announcing superseded request contents; the review link resolves the current authorized review state.',
+      'Messages contain only minimal identifying information and a protected review link, not full proposed profiles, verification secrets, or passwords.',
+      'Notification recipients must authenticate and have current Google administrative authority to review; group membership and group roles confer no application permissions.',
+      'Persist necessary delivery state, expose failures, and retry sending without losing/replacing the proposal or repeating completed Google writes. Repeated event processing does not create duplicate logical notification intents.',
+    ],
+  },
+  {
+    n: 21, title: 'Remove expired signup requests through daily cleanup', deps: [6, 9], stories: '27, 66',
+    build: 'Add protected daily cleanup of expired unreviewed signup requests and their no-longer-needed verification data. Demonstrate removal through the administrator queue and persisted records while preserving accepted provisioning and handover work.',
+    criteria: [
+      'A protected scheduled operation removes signup requests whose 30-day unreviewed lifetime has expired, along with their obsolete applicant/verification data.',
+      'Cleanup is safe under duplicate, concurrent, delayed, or missed invocations; no always-on worker or continuous polling is introduced.',
+      'Expired requests cannot be viewed as actionable or approved even before cleanup runs; the existing read/action expiry protection remains authoritative.',
+      'Cleanup racing with acceptance does not remove accepted provisioning progress, account handover data, or records required to recover external operations.',
+      'The administrator queue no longer exposes removed applicant data, and unrelated active requests and minimal completed-account records remain intact.',
+      'Configure the daily invocation within the serverless deployment model and protect its entry point against unauthenticated public triggering.',
+    ],
+  },
+  {
+    n: 22, title: 'Deploy the own-profile journey on Vercel and Neon', type: 'HITL', deps: [1], stories: '29–31, 39, 65, 67–68',
+    build: 'Deploy and demonstrate the first real Workspace-user journey on Vercel with Neon Free Postgres. An operator supplies organization-specific credentials, completes the isolated reader connection, and validates Google-backed sign-in and private own-profile display in the deployed application. This can run early while later AFK slices continue.',
+    criteria: [
+      'Configure the actual Workspace organization, Google OAuth consent/callbacks, isolated backend read-only grant, protected application secrets, Neon database, and Vercel deployment without committing credentials.',
+      'Apply the actual Drizzle schema/migrations and demonstrate organizational Google sign-in, own-profile display, and sign-out through the deployed browser interface.',
+      'Use controlled accounts to verify wrong-organization rejection, cross-user privacy, relevant Users Read/OU restrictions, and suspended/deleted-account access handling.',
+      'Validate reader OAuth revocation/reconnection without accumulating Directory write grants or silently switching identities.',
+      'The application uses serverless/on-demand execution and Neon scale-to-zero without an always-on worker. Document manual provider-tier/allowance management without implementing billing or automatic upgrades.',
+      'Record the accepted native Neon recovery arrangement, including the currently documented Free six-hour restore window; independent backups remain out of scope.',
+      'Record reproducible deployment/verification results and any concrete failure needing implementation follow-up, without exposing secrets or creating new product decisions.',
+    ],
+  },
+  {
+    n: 23, title: 'Verify the complete lifecycle against the actual Workspace organization', type: 'HITL', deps: Array.from({ length: 21 }, (_, i) => i + 2), stories: 'Integration verification across slices 1–22 and their mapped parent user stories',
+    build: 'Complete the live-tenant integration acceptance for the deployed application using controlled test applicants, Workspace accounts, and groups. Verify the actual Google capabilities that controlled browser-test responses cannot establish, resolve concrete integration failures, and record reproducible results.',
+    criteria: [
+      'Demonstrate verified signup, review notification, acceptance/rejection, selected initial memberships, manual Google reset-email account handover, outcome notification, and applicant-data removal end to end.',
+      'Verify intended delegated-administrator account-creation authority and relevant role/OU restrictions. If Google denies creation, use an appropriately privileged acting administrator for that operation; never silently escalate or use domain-wide delegation.',
+      'Demonstrate private own-profile reads, phone and verified-email proposals, replacement during review, whole-request decisions, preserved unrelated contact/recovery data, and current-authority enforcement.',
+      'Verify live group creation/edit/deletion and direct member/manager/owner support, including Groups for Business availability; group roles and notification-group membership do not authorize application administration.',
+      'Validate dedicated sender grant isolation, review-group posting/subscription delivery, protected review links, outcome sending, and revocation/reconnection behavior without revealing credentials.',
+      'Demonstrate suspension/unsuspension and explicitly confirmed deletion only for controlled test accounts after manual data disposition, including denial of previously active application sessions.',
+      'Verify deployment scheduling/expiry and recovery behavior where safely reproducible; preserve recoverable progress under failures and avoid claiming exactly-once delivery or distributed atomicity.',
+      'Record actual tenant capabilities and evidence. Fix integration failures with the existing authorization boundaries, rerun relevant browser checks plus lint/format/build, and leave no test-account passwords or unnecessary applicant data behind.',
+    ],
+  },
+];
+
+assert.equal(slices.length, 23);
+assert.equal(slices.filter((s) => s.type === 'HITL').length, 2);
+for (const slice of slices) {
+  assert(slice.deps.every((n) => n < slice.n), `Slice ${slice.n} is not in dependency order`);
+}
+
+const standard = [
+  'Deliver a demoable end-to-end path through the existing shadcn/Tailwind browser UI, server validation/authorization, required protected persistence, and Google operations. Reuse prior slices; add no authoritative Google-data mirror, local administrator roles, speculative abstractions, or manually authored UI CSS.',
+  'Add runnable behavior checks through the approved running-application browser seam, using isolated real Postgres with actual Drizzle migrations and controlled external Google identity/OAuth/Directory/Gmail responses as relevant. Cover success, access denial, and the concurrency/failure cases above without production auth bypasses or assertions on private implementation structure.',
+  'Repository lint, formatting, build, and relevant browser workflow checks pass. Follow the parent specification, agreed glossary/ADRs, installed Next.js documentation, and repository worktree/stacked-PR workflow.',
+];
+
+const issues = () => json('issue', 'list', '--repo', repo, '--state', 'all', '--limit', '100', '--json', 'number,title,body,labels,state,url');
+const findSlice = (all, slice) => all.filter((issue) => issue.title === slice.title && issue.body.includes(parentUrl));
+const bodyFor = (slice, published) => {
+  const type = slice.type ?? 'AFK';
+  const blockers = slice.deps.length
+    ? slice.deps.map((n) => `- ${published.get(n).url}`).join('\n')
+    : 'None - can start immediately';
+  const criteria = type === 'AFK' ? [...slice.criteria, ...standard] : slice.criteria;
+  return `## Parent\n\n${parentUrl}\n\n## What to build\n\n**Type:** ${type}  \n**User stories covered:** ${slice.stories} (parent #1).\n\n${slice.build}\n\n${type === 'HITL' ? 'Requires an organization operator for live credentials, configuration, or tenant verification. Preserve all parent privacy/authorization boundaries and use controlled test resources.' : 'Use the parent’s approved application-level testing seam and Google-authoritative domain model. This issue is a complete behavioral slice, not a separate schema, API, UI, or test layer.'}\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n${criteria.map((criterion) => `- [ ] ${criterion}`).join('\n')}\n\n## Blocked by\n\n${blockers}\n`;
+};
+
+function publish() {
+  const before = parent();
+  const expected = fingerprint(before);
+  console.log(`Parent baseline fingerprint: ${expected}`);
+  const labels = json('label', 'list', '--repo', repo, '--limit', '100', '--json', 'name');
+  if (!labels.some((label) => label.name === 'ready-for-human')) {
+    gh('label', 'create', 'ready-for-human', '--repo', repo, '--description', 'Fully specified, requires human implementation or live verification', '--color', 'D4C5F9');
+    console.log('Created canonical ready-for-human label.');
+  }
+  const existing = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(existing, slice);
+    assert(matches.length <= 1, `Duplicate matching issues for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    const body = bodyFor(slice, published);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    let issue;
+    if (matches.length) {
+      issue = matches[0];
+      assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), body.trim(), `Existing slice ${slice.n} differs; inspect before changing`);
+      assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label));
+      console.log(`Reusing slice ${slice.n}: ${issue.url}`);
+    } else {
+      const url = gh('issue', 'create', '--repo', repo, '--title', slice.title, '--body', body, '--label', 'enhancement', '--label', label);
+      const number = Number(url.split('/').at(-1));
+      assert(Number.isInteger(number) && number !== 1, `Unexpected created issue URL: ${url}`);
+      issue = { number, url };
+      console.log(`Created slice ${slice.n} (${slice.type ?? 'AFK'}): ${url}`);
+    }
+    const data = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}`);
+    issue.databaseId = data.id;
+    published.set(slice.n, issue);
+    if (slice.deps.length) {
+      const current = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+      for (const n of slice.deps) {
+        const blocker = published.get(n);
+        if (!current.some((value) => value.id === blocker.databaseId)) {
+          gh('api', '--method', 'POST', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`, '-F', `issue_id=${blocker.databaseId}`);
+        }
+      }
+      console.log(`  Native blockers: ${slice.deps.map((n) => `#${published.get(n).number}`).join(', ')}`);
+    }
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed during publication');
+  console.log(`Published ${published.size} slices; parent #1 unchanged. Verification fingerprint: ${expected}`);
+}
+
+function verify(expected) {
+  assert(expected, 'Supply the baseline parent fingerprint');
+  const all = issues();
+  const published = new Map();
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const matches = findSlice(all, slice);
+    assert.equal(matches.length, 1, `Expected exactly one issue for slice ${slice.n}`);
+    published.set(slice.n, matches[0]);
+  }
+  let edges = 0;
+  for (const slice of slices) {
+    const issue = published.get(slice.n);
+    assert.equal(issue.state, 'OPEN', `Slice ${slice.n} is not open`);
+    assert.equal(issue.body.trim(), bodyFor(slice, published).trim(), `Slice ${slice.n} body mismatch`);
+    const label = slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-human' : 'ready-for-agent';
+    assert(issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === label), `Slice ${slice.n} triage mismatch`);
+    assert(!issue.labels.some((value) => value.name === (slice.type === 'HITL' ? 'ready-for-agent' : 'ready-for-human')));
+    const deps = json('api', `repos/${repo}/issues/${issue.number}/dependencies/blocked_by`);
+    assert.deepEqual(deps.map((value) => value.number).sort((a, b) => a - b), slice.deps.map((n) => published.get(n).number).sort((a, b) => a - b), `Slice ${slice.n} native dependency mismatch`);
+    edges += deps.length;
+    console.log(`Verified ${slice.n}. #${issue.number}: ${issue.title} [${label}]`);
+  }
+  assert.equal(fingerprint(parent()), expected, 'Parent issue changed');
+  console.log(`Verified ${published.size} open issues, 21 AFK + 2 HITL, ${edges} native dependency edges, exact template bodies, and unchanged parent #1.`);
+}
+
+if (process.argv[2] === 'publish') publish();
+else if (process.argv[2] === 'verify') verify(process.argv[3]);
+else throw new Error('Use publish or verify <parent-fingerprint>');

parts.text:
Published **23 issues** with acceptance criteria, user-story coverage, and **46 verified native dependency links**.

- **AFK:** #2–#22, labeled `ready-for-agent`.
- **HITL:** [deployment #23](https://github.com/itsmeyaw/binden/issues/23) and [live integration verification #24](https://github.com/itsmeyaw/binden/issues/24), labeled `ready-for-human`.

Start with [#2: Sign in and view your own Workspace profile](https://github.com/itsmeyaw/binden/issues/2). Parent #1 is unchanged.

## Objective
- Publish the user-approved breakdown of Google Workspace specification #1 into 23 independently verifiable vertical-slice GitHub issues.
- Publish blockers first, apply AFK/HITL triage labels, verify dependencies and bodies, and leave parent #1 unchanged.

## Important Details
- Repository: `itsmeyaw/binden`; canonical parent: https://github.com/itsmeyaw/binden/issues/1, title `Google Workspace onboarding, self-service, and administration`, labels `enhancement`, `ready-for-agent`.
- User approved the specification, browser-facing testing seam, and latest 23-slice breakdown with “lgtm.” No further approval is needed before publication.
- User’s `/to-issues` requirements:
  - Thin vertical slices spanning working UI, server behavior, required persistence/Google operations, and tests; each demoable/verifiable independently.
  - Prefer AFK; HITL for live operator/configuration/tenant work.
  - Exact child body headings: `## Parent`, `## What to build`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Blocked by`.
  - Use real blocking issue references, publish in dependency order.
  - Avoid specific source paths/code snippets in child descriptions.
  - **Do NOT close or modify parent #1**, including comments/labels.
- Tracker conventions already read; no setup skill needed. Use `gh` CLI.
- Label mapping: AFK → `ready-for-agent`; HITL → `ready-for-human`.
  - GitHub currently has `ready-for-agent`, but **does not yet have `ready-for-human`**.
  - Publication script creates missing `ready-for-human`, description `Fully specified, requires human implementation or live verification`, color `D4C5F9`.
- Approved slices; numbers are proposal IDs, **not yet GitHub issue numbers**:
